title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem — Reference Architectures, Deployment Guide, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback
author: Aarti Patel
content:
Overview
========
This document is the canonical Redwood Inference reference for private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It combines reference architectures, pre-deployment customer requirements, packaging and installer details, a step-by-step deployment checklist, day-2 operational procedures, and upgrade/rollback playbooks. Use this guide when onboarding new customers, designing reference architectures, or writing runbooks for private installations.

Scope
-----
- Target audiences: Solutions Engineers, Platform Engineers, Customer SREs, and Enterprise IT teams.
- Deployment modes covered: VPC (cloud private control plane + customer VPC), On‑Prem (air-gapped and networked), and Hybrid.
- Day-2 topics: monitoring, alerting, backups, scaling, node lifecycle, and incident playbooks.
- Upgrade and rollback: supported upgrade strategies, DB migration notes, and validated rollback steps.

Owner & Contacts
----------------
- Product owner: Aarti Patel (eng-private-deployments)
- Primary engineering owner: Diego Martinez (serving-runtime)
- Support escalation: private-deployments@redwood.example.com
- Pager: #private-deployments-oncall (Slack)

Reference Architectures (High level)
----------------------------------
1) VPC Deployment (recommended for most enterprise cloud customers)
   - Control plane: Redwood-managed control plane (hosted) or customer-managed control plane in customer VPC (optional).
   - Data plane: Customer VPC with dedicated subnets for inference nodes, autoscaling groups or managed node pools.
   - Networking: Private subnets for nodes, NAT/egress GW for pull updates, Transit Gateway or VPC peering for cross-region routing.
   - Security: Security groups limiting ingress to the control plane and customer application CIDRs; IAM roles for node bootstrap; KMS integration for key material.

2) On‑Prem Deployment (air‑gapped and connected)
   - Packaging: Docker images + offline Helm charts (tarball) or VM appliance for strictly air-gapped installs.
   - Runtime: Kubernetes (1.24+ validated) strongly preferred. For non-K8s, use the provided VM appliance.
   - Storage: Local PVCs for caches, NFS/SMB or object-store (S3-compatible) for model storage.
   - Networking: Internal load balancer, service mesh optional (Istio/Linkerd supported).

3) Hybrid (control plane hosted, data plane on‑prem)
   - Control-plane <-> data-plane communications encrypted over TLS 1.3.
   - Heartbeats and routing policies respect customer network egress rules; fallback to dedicated queues in hosted control plane when connectivity degraded.

Pre-requisites & Customer Requirements (Checklist)
------------------------------------------------
Provide this checklist to customers before scheduling a deployment engagement.

- Identity and Access
  - Admin IAM role (cloud) or local admin user (on-prem) with permissions to create VPC/subnets, SGs, and attach policies.
  - KMS/HSM access method (customer-managed keys recommended).

- Networking
  - VPC: CIDR ranges that do not overlap with Redwood control plane endpoints.
  - Subnet count: Minimum 3 private subnets across >=2 AZs for high-availability.
  - NAT gateways or egress proxies for outbound pulls (images, telemetry).
  - Firewall allowlist: control-plane IP ranges and ports (see Appendix A).

- Compute & Storage Sizing (example guidance)
  - Inference node types: GPU (A10G/A100 equivalent) or CPU (for small workloads).
  - Minimum cluster size (for production): 3 inference nodes + 3 control-plane-runtime nodes + 1 database node.

| Workload profile | Model class | Nodes (GPU) | Estimated peak RPS | Storage (GB) |
|------------------|-------------|------------:|-------------------:|------------:|
| Small (dev/test)  | 7B          | 1‑2         | 5‑20               | 200         |
| Medium (prod)     | 13B‑30B     | 3‑6         | 50‑200             | 500‑2000    |
| Large (high qps)  | 70B+        | 6+          | 200+               | 2000+       |

- Certificates and PKI
  - TLS cert for ingress load balancers and control plane endpoints.
  - Root CA or configured trust bundle in air-gapped installs.

Packaging & Installer
---------------------
- Packaging formats:
  - Kubernetes: Helm chart (redwood-private/<version>.tgz).
  - VM appliance: OVA image + installer script for non-K8s environments.
  - Air-gap: tarball containing container images (OCI layout) and helm charts.

- Versioning & manifests:
  - Use semantic versions: rwinf-X.Y.Z. Example Helm values file is in Appendix B.

- Installer modes:
  - unattended (CI): helm install --create-namespace -f values-prod.yaml redwood-private ./chart
  - interactive: ./install.sh --mode interactive --config customer-config.yaml

Deployment Procedure — VPC (step-by-step)
---------------------------------------
1) Pre-deploy validation (SRE/SE)
   1.1 Confirm CIDR and AZ plan, required IAM roles, and KMS access.
   1.2 Ensure monitoring endpoints and firewall rules are provisioned.
2) Infrastructure provisioning (Terraform)
   2.1 Apply network module (example):

   # terraform snippet (example)
   provider "aws" { region = "us-west-2" }
   module "redwood_vpc" {
     source = "git::ssh://git@repo.internal/infra/modules/vpc.git//redwood?ref=v1.2.0"
     vpc_cidr = "10.10.0.0/16"
     az_count = 3
   }

3) Kubernetes cluster (EKS/GKE/AKS)
   3.1 Create node groups sized for GPU/CPU requirements.
   3.2 Apply node-level security hardening per infra-standards (SSH disabled, restricted IAM).
4) Install Redwood components
   4.1 Pull helm chart and apply production values: helm upgrade --install redwood-private ./chart -f values-prod.yaml --timeout 15m
   4.2 Validate pods: kubectl -n redwood get pods --show-labels | grep -v Running

5) Post-deploy validation and smoke tests
   5.1 Run connection smoke test: curl --cacert /etc/ssl/redwood/ca.pem https://controlplane.example.com/healthz
   5.2 Run inference smoke test against a pinned model: POST /v1/generate with small prompt (see Appendix C).

Deployment Procedure — On‑Prem (air‑gapped)
------------------------------------------
1) Delivery
   1.1 Provide customer with an offline bundle: redwood-offline-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz and signed checksum.
   1.2 Share installation checklist and offline preflight script.
2) On‑site preflight
   2.1 Validate hardware and network isolation.
   2.2 Import root CA and trust bundle into cluster nodes.
3) Install images locally
   3.1 Load OCI images into local registry: ctr images import images.tar
   3.2 Deploy helm chart pointing to local registry (values.yaml -> image.repository: registry.local/redwood).
4) Validation
   4.1 Run offline smoke tests, validate model pulls from local model store.

Day‑2 Operations (Operational runbook)
-------------------------------------
Monitoring & Alerting
- Integrations: Prometheus + Alertmanager, Grafana, and Datadog (optional).
- Key metrics to capture: per-model p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, queue length, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate.
- Recommended alerts (example thresholds):
  - Inference p99 latency > 2s for 5m -> SEV-3
  - Queue depth > 500 requests for 10m -> SEV-2
  - GPU OOM rate > 1 for 1m -> SEV-1

Backups and Persistence
- Database: nightly logical backups of Postgres (pg_dump) retained for 30 days.
- Model artifacts: replicate to S3-compatible storage with versioned prefixes.
- Config and secrets: store in customer KMS or HashiVault; snapshot Helm release values monthly.

Scaling and Capacity Changes
- Horizontal scaling: add nodes to the GPU node pool and cordon/drain for graceful pod rescheduling.
- Autoscaling: recommend Cluster Autoscaler + HPA for stateless workers; set scale-up cooldown 2m and scale-down 10m.

Node maintenance procedure (planned)
1) Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
2) Drain workloads gracefully: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
3) Perform OS/kernel updates per customer maintenance window
4) Uncordon node: kubectl uncordon <node>

Upgrade & Rollback Playbook
---------------------------
Supported upgrade paths: patch (X.Y.Z -> X.Y.Z+N), minor (X.Y -> X.(Y+1)), and major (requires engineering release notes and migration window). Always test upgrades in a staging cluster that mirrors production.

Canary upgrade (recommended for large fleets)
1) Create a canary release by updating Helm values to route 5‑10% of traffic to the new version.
2) Monitor latency, error rate, and model output quality for 30‑60 minutes.
3) If metrics are within thresholds, increase rollout to 50% then 100%.

Blue/Green strategy (zero-downtime)
1) Deploy new release to a parallel namespace redwood-green.
2) Run smoke and integration tests against redwood-green.
3) Switch ingress (LB weight or DNS) to green namespace in a controlled window.
4) Keep blue for 24‑72 hours as warm fallback.

Rollback steps (emergency)
1) If immediate rollback required, run: helm rollback redwood-private <previous_revision> -n redwood
2) If DB migrations were applied and are incompatible, follow DB rollback runbook (see related_pages).
3) Re-instate previous routing weights and monitor for errors.

Validation & Health Checks
-------------------------
Smoke-tests (automated)
- Health endpoint: GET /healthz (should return 200 + JSON {"status":"ok"}).
- Inference correctness: Run a scripted prompt set (Appendix C) and verify top-1 response contains expected tokens for golden prompts.
SLOs to target (customer-facing)
- Inference p95 latency: <= 500ms for small models; <= 1.5s for mid-size models.
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for Dedicated/Private production installs.

Appendix A — Network Ports & Endpoints (example)
------------------------------------------------
| Service component | Port | Direction | Notes |
| Control plane API | 443  | inbound from customer-admins | TLS required |
| Node agent        | 8080 | outbound to control-plane | ephemeral certs |
| Metrics exporter  | 9100 | inbound from Prometheus | metrics endpoint |

Appendix B — Example Helm values (trimmed)
-----------------------------------------
replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: registry.redwood.internal/redwood-private
  tag: rwinf-1.4.2
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: "2000m"
    memory: "8Gi"
  limits:
    cpu: "4000m"
    memory: "16Gi"
nodeSelector:
  node-role.kubernetes.io/inference: "true"
service:
  type: ClusterIP
  port: 443

Appendix C — Smoke test example (curl)
-------------------------------------
curl -s -X POST https://controlplane.example.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwinf-small-7b","input":"Say hello in 3 languages."}'

Troubleshooting (common issues)
-------------------------------
- Pods stuck Pending: verify node selectors and GPU drivers are installed.
- Image pull errors in air-gapped: ensure local registry has the images and credentials in imagePullSecrets.
- Slow cold-starts: enable KV cache warmers and pre-warm frequently-used models.

Appendix D — Example Terraform outputs to share with customer
-----------------------------------------------------------
- vpc_id: vpc-0abc123def
- subnets: [subnet-0123, subnet-0456, subnet-0789]
- cluster_name: redwood-prod-eks

Ownership, SLA & Handover
-------------------------
- Handover checklist must be completed before project sign-off:
  - Access and trust bundle delivered
  - Runbooks present in customer wiki
  - Backup and restore tested (DR drill)
- SLA: 99.9% availability for production clusters; escalation matrix attached to contract.
